title: Sebastian and the Compass
premise: Ines Delacroix, a pearl diver's child indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has survived by being useful and unseen in the company's chart workshop. When a gaunt stranger named Sebastian arrives bearing a letter in the unmistakable hand of Master Alaric—the cartographer who drowned two years ago—Ines learns the old man faked his death to finish a forbidden atlas mapping the company's smuggled routes. The letter names Ines as his apprentice and heir to the work. As company inspectors close in on the workshop, Ines and Sebastian race to complete and hide the atlas, ending with Ines choosing exile over safety: she sends the atlas out with Sebastian while staying behind to face the company, no longer invisible but finally belonging to something worth the price.
about_author: Bram Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trade ledgers before turning to fiction. They write stories about the people history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines grinding pigments and mending charts in the Meridian workshop, invisible among indentured workers, haunted by the memory of Master Alaric's drowning. A routine inventory reveals a locked drawer Alaric left bearing Ines's name. Emotional beat: the ache of being unclaimed, and the first crack in Ines's careful anonymity.

chapters.title: A Letter from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sebastian arrives at dusk, half-starved, carrying Alaric's letter naming Ines heir to an unfinished atlas that could hang the company. Ines refuses—until inspectors announce a full audit of the workshop within the month. Emotional beat: terror giving way to reluctant purpose; found family begins with shared danger.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ines and Sebastian. Working nights, they decode Alaric's ciphered coastlines while the audit looms and a jealous foreman grows suspicious. Sebastian confesses he was Alaric's courier—and the reason the company hunted him. Emotional beat: trust forged through confession, as survival starts costing them their caution.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. The foreman betrays them; the workshop is raided mid-completion. Ines hides the finished atlas in a hollowed diving bell from her father's boat and sends it to sea with Sebastian, then stays behind to take the blame. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve—Ines loses her hiding place and gains a self worth being seen for.
